description.content:
ExecutionService provides access to workflow executions — runs of a
 bioinformatics workflow that process instrument data. Listing and reading
 execution metadata requires the "executions:read" scope; listing files and
 obtaining download credentials requires "executions:download"; retrieving
 logs requires "executions:logs".

List executions accessible to the authenticated tenant, optionally
 filtered.

query.description:
Search and filter expression. Space-separated `keyword:value` terms are
 ANDed together; bare text with no keyword searches all string fields. For
 date fields, replace the colon with a comparison operator (`>=`, `<=`,
 `>`, `<`, `!=`). List alternatives for one keyword with commas, e.g.
 `status:running,pending`. Dates accept ISO-8601 or relative offsets such
 as `24h`, `7d`, or `1mo`.

 Filterable keywords:

 - **String:** `name`, `input.run.id`, `input.run.name`, `input.run.instrument_name`, `input.execution.id`, `input.execution.name`, `flow.name`, `workflow.name`, `started_by`
 - **Enum:** `status`, `platform` (`aws_omics`, `seqera`, `dnanexus`, `catalyst`), `output.kind` (`fastq`, `bam`, `vcf`, `cram`, `parquet`)
 - **Date:** `time_created`, `time_started`, `time_completed`, `time_updated`

 Examples:

 - `workflow.name:bases2fastq status:running`
 - `platform:seqera output.kind:fastq time_completed>=24h`
Maximum number of executions to return (default: 100, max: 1000)
If true, include total_count in the response (adds a count query)

Get temporary, read-only S3 credentials scoped to an execution's storage
 location. Use these for bulk or repeated downloads via the AWS CLI or SDK
 instead of per-object presigned URLs.

query.description:
Optional path prefix within the execution to scope credentials to.
 Execution-relative, identical semantics to
 ListExecutionFilesRequest.prefix. ".." segments are rejected.
 When omitted, credentials are scoped to the whole execution (the
 execution root).

Lifetime of the returned credentials, in seconds. Optional; defaults to
 1 hour (when 0 or unset). Minimum 900s. Capped by AWS: up to 36h (129600s)
 for federation-token connections, or the role's MaxSessionDuration (12h
 typical) for role-backed connections. Values below the minimum or above the
 cap are rejected.

List the files produced by an execution, drawn from the execution's
 storage location.

query.description:
Path prefix within the execution, e.g. "visualization/" or "Stats/foo".
 The execution is a self-contained namespace: paths do not include any
 bucket-level or workflow-level layout. Round-trips with File.path
 returned by this RPC. ".." segments are rejected.
 Optional: when omitted, lists the whole execution (the execution root).

If true, list all files recursively under the prefix (default: true)
 If false, list only files and subdirectories at the current level
Maximum number of files to return per page (default: 1000, max: 1000)
Continuation token from previous response (passthrough from storage)

If true, populate File.download_url (a presigned URL) on each returned
 file. Defaults to false. Set to true only when the caller intends to
 fetch file content from the response: generating presigned URLs has a
 per-object cost and the URLs themselves are credentials with a
 multi-hour lifetime. Use GetExecutionDownloadCredentials when
 long-lived bulk access is required.

Lifetime of the presigned download_url, in seconds. Optional; defaults to
 1 hour. Only applies when include_download_url = true. Max 7 days.

If true, presign each download_url with S3 ChecksumMode=ENABLED so the
 object's stored checksum is returned on the GET (in the
 x-amz-checksum-<algo> response header) and a client can verify download
 integrity in a single streaming pass. Defaults false; has no effect unless
 include_download_url = true. When enabled the presigned URL signs the
 x-amz-checksum-mode request header, so the fetch MUST send
 x-amz-checksum-mode:ENABLED — a plain GET that omits it fails with HTTP
 403. Best-effort: objects stored without a checksum return none.

 Applies only to AWS S3-backed storage connections; other storage backends
 do not presign S3 GETs and silently ignore this field.

info.name: Element Biosciences Cloud Execution Service API

description.content:
The Element Biosciences Cloud API provides programmatic access to data in
the Element Biosciences Cloud platform: instrument runs (sequencing and
multiomics), workflow executions, registered instruments, storage
connections, and the files those resources produce.

All paths are versioned under `/v1`.

## Authentication
Every request must include an API key in the `x-api-key` header. Create and
manage keys in the Element Biosciences Cloud console. Call `GET /v1/auth` to
confirm which tenant a key belongs to.

## Scopes
Each API key carries one or more scopes of the form
`resource:action[:resource_id]`, for example `runs:read`,
`executions:download`, or `storage:download:{connection_id}`. A request that
is authenticated but lacks the required scope fails with HTTP 403 and the
`INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE` reason. List endpoints transparently restrict results
to the resources a key is scoped to.

## Pagination
List endpoints are cursor-paginated. Set `page_size` to control the page
length and pass the `next_page_token` from one response as the `page_token`
of the next; an empty `next_page_token` indicates the last page.

## Errors
Errors return a JSON body with an integer `code`, a human-readable
`message`, and a `details` array. Each detail carries a machine-readable
`reason` (for example `RUN_NOT_FOUND` or `INVALID_API_KEY`) and the
`domain` `cloud-api.elembio.io`. The `request_id` in the detail metadata
matches the `X-Request-ID` response header; include it when reporting
problems.


Contact Support:
 Name: Element Biosciences
